designProvenance.statement: No exact local product-brief section 6.4 text or authoritative 11-state AED taxonomy was available. The state labels, branch identifiers and new error codes are Phase 3B project-authored organisation; every clinical behaviour is constrained by the cited source-checked fact extract.
designProvenance.newCriticalErrorCodeStatement: Every critical-error code other than unsafe.contact_during_aed_analysis is project-authored as the inverse of a cited source rule; none is represented as recovered section-6.4 wording.
designProvenance.randomisationInvariant: Randomisation selects exactly one listed three-analysis outcome sequence. It never changes DRSABC order, scene-safety rules, breathing decisions, AED clear checks, shock delivery rules, CPR resumption rules or supported stop conditions.

states.title: Awaiting AED
states.stateDescription: Continue chest compressions with as little interruption as possible while an AED is brought to the casualty.

states.title: Power on
states.stateDescription: Switch on the training AED and follow its prompts; some devices power on when their lid opens.

states.title: Prepare chest
states.stateDescription: Expose and prepare the chest, resolve recognised AED hazards, and keep compressions going wherever possible.

sourceReferences.section: C-5 summary of AED application sequence

states.title: Apply right pad
states.stateDescription: Follow the pad picture and place the right adult pad on the right chest just below the collarbone.

states.title: Apply left pad
states.stateDescription: Follow the pad picture and place the left adult pad below and to the left of the left nipple.

states.title: Connect pads
states.stateDescription: Insert the pad connector when the training AED requires it; recognise that some devices use pre-connected pads.

sourceReferences.section: C-5 summary of AED application sequence

states.title: Analyse — clear
states.stateDescription: When analysis is announced, stop compressions, spread the arms, say “Stay Clear”, and ensure nobody touches the casualty.

states.title: Charge — clear
states.stateDescription: If a shock is advised, keep everybody clear while the AED charges.

states.title: Clear check and shock
states.stateDescription: When prompted, say “Stay Clear”, visually confirm nobody is in contact, and press the shock control firmly.

states.title: No shock advised
states.stateDescription: When no shock is advised, restart continuous chest compressions immediately.

states.title: Resume CPR
states.stateDescription: Immediately resume compressions after either outcome and continue until the AED announces its next analysis, normally after two minutes.

transitions.condition: An AED has been brought to the casualty while compressions continue wherever possible.

feedbackStatements.statement: The AED has arrived. Keep interruptions minimal and switch it on.

sourceReferences.section: C-5 summary of AED application sequence
C-5 summary of AED application sequence

transitions.condition: The AED is on, whether by its power control or an automatic lid-open behaviour.

feedbackStatements.statement: The AED is on. Follow its prompts and prepare the chest.

transitions.condition: The chest is exposed, dry enough for pad adhesion, and recognised hazards at the pad sites have been addressed.

feedbackStatements.statement: Chest preparation is complete. Apply the pads promptly.

transitions.condition: The right pad follows its picture and is below the right collarbone.

feedbackStatements.statement: Right pad placement is complete. Apply the left pad.

transitions.condition: The left pad follows its picture and is below and to the left of the left nipple.

feedbackStatements.statement: Both pads are in position. Connect them if the AED requires a connector step.

transitions.condition: The connector is inserted, or the training AED presents a pre-connected pad configuration.

feedbackStatements.statement: Pads are ready. Stop compressions only when analysis is announced and clear the casualty.

transitions.condition: The selected three-analysis pattern yields a shock outcome for this analysis.

feedbackStatements.statement: A shock is advised. Keep everybody clear while the AED charges.

transitions.condition: The selected three-analysis pattern yields a no-shock outcome for this analysis.

feedbackStatements.statement: No shock is advised. Restart compressions immediately.

transitions.condition: The AED has charged and prompts the rescuer to deliver a shock.

feedbackStatements.statement: Before pressing the shock control, repeat the clear call and visually confirm nobody is touching.

transitions.condition: The prompted shock has been delivered after the clear check.

feedbackStatements.statement: Shock delivered. Restart chest compressions immediately.

transitions.condition: The AED has announced that no shock is advised.

feedbackStatements.statement: Restart continuous chest compressions immediately.

transitions.condition: The AED announces its next analysis after the compression interval.

feedbackStatements.statement: When analysis is announced again, stop compressions and clear the casualty.

sourceReferences.section: C-5 summary of AED application sequence

scenarios.title: Scenario A — Home
scenarios.summary: An integrated adult hands-only CPR and AED simulation in a home setting, with source-constrained branches and a three-analysis AED pattern.

initialConditions: A training manikin represents an unresponsive adult casualty in the home setting.
The 995 interaction is visibly labelled SIMULATION and never places a call.
Scene safety, responder availability, AED distance and breathing presentation are selected from the declared branches before scoring.
The casualty begins on the floor; the learner confirms a firm, flat, supine position before entering the compression branch.
Bystander presence and AED walking distance vary between attempts.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

branchingNodes.prompt: Is the scene safe enough to begin the response?

feedbackStatements.statement: The scene has been checked as safe; continue to the responsiveness and help sequence.
Resolve the danger or move the casualty to a safe, flat, open space before continuing.
Every scenario begins with a danger check.

branchingNodes.prompt: Is another bystander available to help?

feedbackStatements.statement: Direct the bystander to activate 995 and fetch the AED when it is within about a 60-second walk.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

feedbackStatements.statement: Use speaker mode for the simulated 995 call, stay on the line and do not leave the casualty to search for an AED.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

feedbackStatements.statement: The bystander branch changes task allocation, not the clinical sequence.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

branchingNodes.prompt: Is the AED within about a 60-second walk?

feedbackStatements.statement: If another person is available, ask them to fetch the nearby AED; a lone rescuer still stays with the casualty.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

feedbackStatements.statement: Continue the response without sending a lone rescuer away; the simulated dispatcher can help locate an AED and nearby assistance.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

feedbackStatements.statement: AED distance never changes the rule that a lone rescuer remains with the casualty.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

branchingNodes.prompt: What breathing presentation is observed within the 10-second check?

feedbackStatements.statement: Gasping is abnormal breathing; begin CPR and continue the AED response.
Absent, abnormal or uncertain breathing requires immediate CPR.
Do not start compressions; monitor the casualty and wait for EMS.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers
RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

feedbackStatements.statement: Complete the breathing check in no more than 10 seconds and choose the matching path.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

branchingNodes.prompt: What outcome does the selected three-analysis pool provide for this AED analysis?

feedbackStatements.statement: Keep everybody clear during charging and shock delivery, then restart compressions immediately.
When no shock is advised, restart continuous compressions immediately.
The outcome sequence may vary, but analysis clear checks and immediate CPR resumption never change.

criticalActions.title: Assess and secure the scene
criticalActions.actionDescription: Check for danger first. Continue only in a safe setting; if the site is unsafe or unsuitable, move the casualty to a safe, flat, open space as soon as possible.

feedbackStatements.statement: Good scene assessment protects both rescuer and casualty before the response continues.

criticalActions.title: Check responsiveness
criticalActions.actionDescription: Tap the casualty’s shoulders firmly and ask loudly whether they are okay, without violent shaking or unnecessary neck movement.

feedbackStatements.statement: The responsiveness check uses a firm shoulder tap and a loud verbal prompt.

criticalActions.title: Activate emergency help
criticalActions.actionDescription: Use the clearly marked SIMULATION 995 flow. If alone, rehearse speaker mode, stay on the line, and follow the dispatcher; an in-facility emergency response system may be activated where applicable.

feedbackStatements.statement: The simulated call keeps the learner with the casualty and follows dispatcher guidance.

criticalActions.title: Manage AED retrieval
criticalActions.actionDescription: Ask another person to fetch an AED when it is within about a 60-second walk. A lone rescuer stays with the casualty and does not leave to search.

feedbackStatements.statement: AED retrieval must never send a lone rescuer away from the casualty.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

criticalActions.title: Check normal breathing
criticalActions.actionDescription: Look for chest rise and fall for no more than 10 seconds. Gasping is not normal breathing; absent, abnormal or uncertain breathing leads to CPR, while normal breathing leads to continued monitoring.

feedbackStatements.statement: The breathing decision separates the monitoring path from the immediate-CPR path.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers
RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

criticalActions.title: Position for CPR
criticalActions.actionDescription: For the CPR branch, place the casualty on their back on a firm, flat surface, supporting the head, neck and body together if a turn is needed.

feedbackStatements.statement: A firm, flat, supine position supports effective compressions.

criticalActions.title: Perform hands-only compressions
criticalActions.actionDescription: For absent, abnormal or uncertain breathing, compress over the lower half of the sternum and avoid the xiphoid process; maintain 100–120 compressions per minute, full recoil and minimal interruptions.

feedbackStatements.statement: Keep placement, rhythm, recoil and interruptions within the source-backed adult practice rules.

criticalActions.title: Prepare and apply the AED
criticalActions.actionDescription: Keep compressions going wherever possible while powering on, resolving hazards, preparing the chest, applying the right then left adult pads, and connecting the pads when required.

feedbackStatements.statement: The AED sequence preserves compressions while preparation and pad placement are completed.

sourceReferences.section: C-5 summary of AED application sequence
C-5 summary of AED application sequence

criticalActions.title: Clear for analysis and shock
criticalActions.actionDescription: Stop compressions when analysis is announced and ensure nobody touches the casualty. If a shock is advised, keep clear during charging, repeat the clear call, visually check contact, then press the shock control when prompted.

feedbackStatements.statement: Nobody touches the casualty during AED analysis, charging or shock delivery.

criticalActions.title: Resume CPR after the AED decision
criticalActions.actionDescription: Restart chest compressions immediately after a delivered shock or a no-shock announcement and continue until the next AED analysis or another supported stop condition.

feedbackStatements.statement: Both AED outcomes return directly to chest compressions.

criticalActions.title: Communicate clearly
criticalActions.actionDescription: Give the simulated dispatcher the requested incident details, follow the coaching, and use an audible clear call before analysis and any shock.

feedbackStatements.statement: Clear spoken communication supports dispatcher guidance and the AED no-touch checks.

criticalActions.title: Minimise avoidable delay
criticalActions.actionDescription: Move through recognition, compressions and AED use without avoidable delay while preserving every scene-safety and no-touch check.

feedbackStatements.statement: Prompt action matters, but speed never removes a required safety or clear check.

criticalActions.title: Monitor normal breathing
criticalActions.actionDescription: On the normal-breathing branch, do not start compressions; continue monitoring and wait for EMS.

feedbackStatements.statement: Normal breathing leads to monitoring rather than chest compressions.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers
RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

criticalErrors.title: Unsafe scene not mitigated
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner continues the response in an unsafe or unsuitable location without first making the setting safe.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the danger check and make or move to a safe, flat, open space before continuing.

feedbackStatements.statement: Pause the attempt and repeat the danger decision before any further clinical action.

criticalErrors.title: Responsiveness not checked
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner bypasses the firm shoulder-tap and loud verbal responsiveness check.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the response sequence from the responsiveness check without violent shaking.

feedbackStatements.statement: Confirm responsiveness before moving to activation and breathing assessment.

criticalErrors.title: Emergency help not activated
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner does not rehearse calling 995 or activating the applicable in-facility response system for an unresponsive casualty.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the SIMULATION activation step, using speaker mode when alone and following dispatcher guidance.

feedbackStatements.statement: The emergency response must be activated as part of DRSABC.

criticalErrors.title: Lone rescuer leaves for an AED
criticalErrors.errorDescription: On the alone branch, the learner leaves the casualty to search for an AED.
criticalErrors.remediation: Stay with the casualty; use speaker mode for the simulated 995 call and ask another person to fetch the AED when one becomes available.

feedbackStatements.statement: A lone rescuer must remain with the casualty rather than leaving to search for an AED.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED
2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

criticalErrors.title: Gasping treated as normal breathing
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner interprets gasping as normal breathing and withholds chest compressions.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the breathing branch: gasping is abnormal and requires immediate CPR.

feedbackStatements.statement: Gasping is not the normal-breathing branch.

criticalErrors.title: Compressions started during normal breathing
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner starts chest compressions after identifying that the casualty is breathing normally.
criticalErrors.remediation: Use the monitoring branch when breathing is normal and wait for EMS.

feedbackStatements.statement: Do not start compressions when normal breathing is present.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers
RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

criticalErrors.title: Compression over the xiphoid area
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner places the compression target over the xiphoid process rather than the lower half of the sternum.
criticalErrors.remediation: Reset hand placement to the centre of the chest over the lower half of the sternum and avoid the xiphoid process.

feedbackStatements.statement: Correct the hand-placement zone before resuming the practice sequence.

criticalErrors.title: Adult pads placed incorrectly
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner does not follow the adult pad pictures or places either pad outside the supported right-chest and left-chest positions.
criticalErrors.remediation: Reapply the right pad below the right collarbone and the left pad below and left of the left nipple, following the pad pictures.

feedbackStatements.statement: Reset the adult pads to the source-backed positions before analysis.

criticalErrors.title: Contact during AED analysis
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner or another person remains in contact with the casualty while the AED is analysing.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the analysis clear sequence: stop compressions, spread the arms, say “Stay Clear”, and confirm nobody is touching.

feedbackStatements.statement: AED analysis requires a complete no-touch clear check.

criticalErrors.title: Shock attempted without a clear check
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner presses the shock control without first keeping everybody clear, repeating the clear call and visually confirming no contact.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat charging and shock delivery with nobody touching and a visible clear check before pressing the control.

feedbackStatements.statement: Never deliver the prompted shock while anybody is touching the casualty.

criticalErrors.title: CPR not resumed after AED outcome
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner delays or omits restarting chest compressions after a delivered shock or a no-shock announcement.
criticalErrors.remediation: Restart compressions immediately after either AED outcome.

feedbackStatements.statement: Both shock and no-shock paths require an immediate return to compressions.

criticalErrors.title: CPR stopped without a supported condition
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner stops CPR when there is no emergency-team takeover, AED analysis/charging/shock prompt, waking, or return of normal breathing.
criticalErrors.remediation: Continue CPR until one of the source-backed stop conditions occurs.

feedbackStatements.statement: Do not end compressions for an unsupported reason.
Use the same DRSABC clinical sequence regardless of the environment or randomised AED outcomes.
If breathing is normal, monitor and wait for EMS rather than starting compressions.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

feedbackStatements.statement: Every analysis, charge and prompted shock retains the no-touch clear requirement.
After shock or no-shock advice, return to compressions immediately.

sourceReferences.section: 2.2 (A) Ask someone to get an AED

criticalActions.title: Assess and secure the scene
criticalActions.actionDescription: Check for danger first. Continue only in a safe setting; if the site is unsafe or unsuitable, move the casualty to a safe, flat, open space as soon as possible.

feedbackStatements.statement: Good scene assessment protects both rescuer and casualty before the response continues.

criticalActions.title: Check responsiveness
criticalActions.actionDescription: Tap the casualty’s shoulders firmly and ask loudly whether they are okay, without violent shaking or unnecessary neck movement.

feedbackStatements.statement: The responsiveness check uses a firm shoulder tap and a loud verbal prompt.

criticalActions.title: Activate emergency help
criticalActions.actionDescription: Use the clearly marked SIMULATION 995 flow. If alone, rehearse speaker mode, stay on the line, and follow the dispatcher; an in-facility emergency response system may be activated where applicable.

feedbackStatements.statement: The simulated call keeps the learner with the casualty and follows dispatcher guidance.

criticalActions.title: Manage AED retrieval
criticalActions.actionDescription: Ask another person to fetch an AED when it is within about a 60-second walk. A lone rescuer stays with the casualty and does not leave to search.

feedbackStatements.statement: AED retrieval must never send a lone rescuer away from the casualty.

criticalActions.title: Check normal breathing
criticalActions.actionDescription: Look for chest rise and fall for no more than 10 seconds. Gasping is not normal breathing; absent, abnormal or uncertain breathing leads to CPR, while normal breathing leads to continued monitoring.

feedbackStatements.statement: The breathing decision separates the monitoring path from the immediate-CPR path.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers
RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

criticalActions.title: Position for CPR
criticalActions.actionDescription: For the CPR branch, place the casualty on their back on a firm, flat surface, supporting the head, neck and body together if a turn is needed.

feedbackStatements.statement: A firm, flat, supine position supports effective compressions.

criticalActions.title: Perform hands-only compressions
criticalActions.actionDescription: For absent, abnormal or uncertain breathing, compress over the lower half of the sternum and avoid the xiphoid process; maintain 100–120 compressions per minute, full recoil and minimal interruptions.

feedbackStatements.statement: Keep placement, rhythm, recoil and interruptions within the source-backed adult practice rules.

criticalActions.title: Prepare and apply the AED
criticalActions.actionDescription: Keep compressions going wherever possible while powering on, resolving hazards, preparing the chest, applying the right then left adult pads, and connecting the pads when required.

feedbackStatements.statement: The AED sequence preserves compressions while preparation and pad placement are completed.

sourceReferences.section: C-5 summary of AED application sequence
C-5 summary of AED application sequence

criticalActions.title: Clear for analysis and shock
criticalActions.actionDescription: Stop compressions when analysis is announced and ensure nobody touches the casualty. If a shock is advised, keep clear during charging, repeat the clear call, visually check contact, then press the shock control when prompted.

feedbackStatements.statement: Nobody touches the casualty during AED analysis, charging or shock delivery.

criticalActions.title: Resume CPR after the AED decision
criticalActions.actionDescription: Restart chest compressions immediately after a delivered shock or a no-shock announcement and continue until the next AED analysis or another supported stop condition.

feedbackStatements.statement: Both AED outcomes return directly to chest compressions.

criticalActions.title: Communicate clearly
criticalActions.actionDescription: Give the simulated dispatcher the requested incident details, follow the coaching, and use an audible clear call before analysis and any shock.

feedbackStatements.statement: Clear spoken communication supports dispatcher guidance and the AED no-touch checks.

criticalActions.title: Minimise avoidable delay
criticalActions.actionDescription: Move through recognition, compressions and AED use without avoidable delay while preserving every scene-safety and no-touch check.

feedbackStatements.statement: Prompt action matters, but speed never removes a required safety or clear check.

criticalActions.title: Monitor normal breathing
criticalActions.actionDescription: On the normal-breathing branch, do not start compressions; continue monitoring and wait for EMS.

feedbackStatements.statement: Normal breathing leads to monitoring rather than chest compressions.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers
RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

criticalErrors.title: Unsafe scene not mitigated
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner continues the response in an unsafe or unsuitable location without first making the setting safe.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the danger check and make or move to a safe, flat, open space before continuing.

feedbackStatements.statement: Pause the attempt and repeat the danger decision before any further clinical action.

criticalErrors.title: Responsiveness not checked
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner bypasses the firm shoulder-tap and loud verbal responsiveness check.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the response sequence from the responsiveness check without violent shaking.

feedbackStatements.statement: Confirm responsiveness before moving to activation and breathing assessment.

criticalErrors.title: Emergency help not activated
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner does not rehearse calling 995 or activating the applicable in-facility response system for an unresponsive casualty.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the SIMULATION activation step, using speaker mode when alone and following dispatcher guidance.

feedbackStatements.statement: The emergency response must be activated as part of DRSABC.

criticalErrors.title: Lone rescuer leaves for an AED
criticalErrors.errorDescription: On the alone branch, the learner leaves the casualty to search for an AED.
criticalErrors.remediation: Stay with the casualty; use speaker mode for the simulated 995 call and ask another person to fetch the AED when one becomes available.

feedbackStatements.statement: A lone rescuer must remain with the casualty rather than leaving to search for an AED.

criticalErrors.title: Gasping treated as normal breathing
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner interprets gasping as normal breathing and withholds chest compressions.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the breathing branch: gasping is abnormal and requires immediate CPR.

feedbackStatements.statement: Gasping is not the normal-breathing branch.

criticalErrors.title: Compressions started during normal breathing
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner starts chest compressions after identifying that the casualty is breathing normally.
criticalErrors.remediation: Use the monitoring branch when breathing is normal and wait for EMS.

feedbackStatements.statement: Do not start compressions when normal breathing is present.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers
RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

criticalErrors.title: Compression over the xiphoid area
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner places the compression target over the xiphoid process rather than the lower half of the sternum.
criticalErrors.remediation: Reset hand placement to the centre of the chest over the lower half of the sternum and avoid the xiphoid process.

feedbackStatements.statement: Correct the hand-placement zone before resuming the practice sequence.

criticalErrors.title: Adult pads placed incorrectly
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner does not follow the adult pad pictures or places either pad outside the supported right-chest and left-chest positions.
criticalErrors.remediation: Reapply the right pad below the right collarbone and the left pad below and left of the left nipple, following the pad pictures.

feedbackStatements.statement: Reset the adult pads to the source-backed positions before analysis.

criticalErrors.title: Contact during AED analysis
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner or another person remains in contact with the casualty while the AED is analysing.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat the analysis clear sequence: stop compressions, spread the arms, say “Stay Clear”, and confirm nobody is touching.

feedbackStatements.statement: AED analysis requires a complete no-touch clear check.

criticalErrors.title: Shock attempted without a clear check
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner presses the shock control without first keeping everybody clear, repeating the clear call and visually confirming no contact.
criticalErrors.remediation: Repeat charging and shock delivery with nobody touching and a visible clear check before pressing the control.

feedbackStatements.statement: Never deliver the prompted shock while anybody is touching the casualty.

criticalErrors.title: CPR not resumed after AED outcome
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner delays or omits restarting chest compressions after a delivered shock or a no-shock announcement.
criticalErrors.remediation: Restart compressions immediately after either AED outcome.

feedbackStatements.statement: Both shock and no-shock paths require an immediate return to compressions.

criticalErrors.title: CPR stopped without a supported condition
criticalErrors.errorDescription: The learner stops CPR when there is no emergency-team takeover, AED analysis/charging/shock prompt, waking, or return of normal breathing.
criticalErrors.remediation: Continue CPR until one of the source-backed stop conditions occurs.

feedbackStatements.statement: Do not end compressions for an unsupported reason.
Use the same DRSABC clinical sequence regardless of the environment or randomised AED outcomes.
If breathing is normal, monitor and wait for EMS rather than starting compressions.

sourceReferences.section: RCA adult BLS algorithm for lay rescuers

feedbackStatements.statement: Every analysis, charge and prompted shock retains the no-touch clear requirement.
After shock or no-shock advice, return to compressions immediately.

scenarios.title: Scenario D — Community facility
scenarios.summary: An integrated adult hands-only CPR and AED simulation in a community facility setting, with source-constrained branches and a three-analysis AED pattern.

initialConditions: A training manikin represents an unresponsive adult casualty in the community facility setting.
The 995 interaction is visibly labelled SIMULATION and never places a call.
Scene safety, responder availability, AED distance and breathing presentation are selected from the declared branches before scoring.
Bystander availability and public-access AED distance vary between attempts.
If the AED is in a break-glass box, the learner uses an object and clears fragments before reaching for the key.
